summary: Unexpected pin retention after canary revert caused by edge cache TTL misalignment
description: Issue summary: Customer NexaHealth observed that after aborting a canary (weight set back to 0 and model roll reverted), a subset of their sessions continued routing to the canary model for up to ~90 minutes. Impact: Incorrect model responses in production for a small percentage (~0.7%) of requests to /v1/chat and /v1/generate, leading to user-facing content mismatches and compliance risk. Environment: dedicated deployment (customer tenant in us-west-2), canary was open-llama-v2-13b-q8 promoted against baseline redwood-alpha-1.0. Observed behavior: After canary revert via console and canary-controller, traffic steering showed 0% canary. However, logs and customer samples show requests still served by open-llama-v2-13b-q8. Expected behavior: After revert, no traffic should be routed to canary model once weight is 0 and route pinning cleared across edge and runtime caches.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start from baseline model A (redwood-alpha-1.0) serving route /v1/chat for tenant nexhealth.
2) Launch canary B (open-llama-v2-13b-q8) and set canary weight to 5% via Console.
3) Observe canary traffic for 30 minutes, then abort rollout and set canary weight to 0 via Console -> canary-controller -> 'revert'.
4) Verify controller reports 0% weight and no active canary in controller logs.
5) Send 10000 synthetic requests with consistent session-id header and inspect model id in responses; note ~0.7% still hit model B for some sessions.
6) Observe that clearing the 'x-redwood-session' header on client side causes immediate routing to baseline model for those sessions.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Edge route cache TTL (default 120s) was not aligned with controller revert window (30s) leading to stale affinity entries that map session IDs to the canary model.
Hypothesis B: Session-affinity pin stored at edge was not automatically invalidated by controller revert event due to missing eviction hook in older edge release (edge v2.3.1).
Evidence: edge-proxy log shows 'route-eviction-notice failed' with ttl_mismatch=120s; controller audit confirms revert at 15:02:04Z.

Reproducibility: Reproduced in a staged repro using synthetic session tokens — when session token persisted across revert and edge cache not flushed, ~0.5-1.0% of traffic remained pinned for up to cache TTL multiples.
Scope: Limited to us-west-2 edge fleet running edge v2.3.1 with default route-cache config. Not observed in eu-west in current rollout.
Temporary mitigation: targeted edge cache flush for tenant keys reduced residuals to near-zero. Short-term customer workaround: rotate/clear SDK session IDs on client.

Long-term action items: implement on-revert eviction hook in canary-controller to send eviction events to edge-proxy; add TTL alignment check to deployment pipeline; add test in canary e2e to validate eviction behavior.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: Performed tenant-scoped cache flush on us-west-2 edge nodes at 2026-03-13T09:34Z which removed most stale pins. Informed customer to rotate session tokens as immediate mitigation.

Fix under development: PR github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6219 implements an on-revert eviction notification to edge-proxy and aligns default TTLs. Pending staged rollout to edge fleet (edge v2.3.4) on 2026-03-15.

Follow-ups: (1) Add canary-revert evict test to CI, (2) Run audit to identify tenants that experienced stale pin >15 minutes, (3) Update runbook: on canary revert, run edge eviction AND notify customer if persisted pins detected.

Customer communication: NexaHealth notified of immediate mitigation and upcoming fix timeline. Customer accepted workaround and asked for post-deploy verification. Assigned follow-up check on 2026-03-16.
Status: Partial mitigation applied; fix merged to staging branch and scheduled for progressive edge rollout. Ticket will be closed after verification window and customer sign-off.
Postmortem action: Track as P1 postmortem candidate if we observe similar events during next 30 days.
